{{nihongo|'''Kagamitsukuri Nimasu Amateru Mitama Shrine'''|鏡作坐天照御魂神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Tawaramoto, Nara|arz|تاواراموتو|ceb|Tawaramoto-chō (subdistrito)|es|Tawaramoto (Nara)|fa|تاواراموتو، نارا|fr|Tawaramoto|hy|Տավարամոտո|it|Tawaramoto|ja|田原本町|ko|다와라모토정|mg|Tawaramoto|ms|Tawaramoto, Nara|my|တဝရမိုတိုမြို့၊ နာရ|pl|Tawaramoto|ru|Таварамото|sv|Tawaramoto|tl|Tawaramoto, Nara|tr|Tawaramoto|uk|Таварамото|ur|ٹاوارا موٹو، نارا|zh|田原本町|qid=Q1203159}}, {{ill|Shiki District, Nara|Q1155036|qid=Q1155036}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai Taisha|Q134917288|qid=Q134917288}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=kensha}}. It is said to have been founded by the Kagamitsukuri-be mirror-making clan, who lived in this area from the 4th to 5th centuries producing mirrors, and enshrined their tutelary deity ({{ill|Amenohoakari|Q10940411|qid=Q10940411|lt=Amateru Kuniteru Hikohokari-no-Mikoto}}) together with their ancestor ({{ill|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|Q6080112|qid=Q6080112|lt=Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto}}). {{nihongo|'''Kagamitsukuri Nimasu Amateru Mitama Shrine'''|鏡作坐天照御魂神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
The three enshrined deities are:
* {{ill|Amenohoakari|Q10940411|qid=Q10940411|lt=Amateru Kuniteru Hikohokari-no-Mikoto}} (あまてるくにてるひこほあかりのみこと)
* {{ill|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|Q6080112|qid=Q6080112|lt=Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto}} (いしこりどめのみこと)
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Nukado}} no Mikoto (あめのぬかどのみこと)

In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Shrines}}, only one deity seat is recorded. Because the shrine name means "the shrine of Amateru Mitama no Kami seated at Kagamitsukuri," it is considered originally a solar-cult shrine devoted to "Amateru Mitama no Kami." == History ==
According to classical chronicles ({{ill|Kiki (Shinto)|Q842308|qid=Q842308}}), in the 6th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}, the deity {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}} enshrined in the {{ill|Tokyo Imperial Palace|Q500681|qid=Q500681}} was moved to the land of Sasanuhi because of reverence. Shrine tradition states: "On the 3rd day of the 9th month in Emperor Sujin's 6th year, mirrors in the form of the sun image were cast in this place (to enshrine in the palace in place of Amaterasu), and made into the divine spirit of Amaterasu; the mirror now in the inner attendants' office is that one. This shrine enshrines the prototype mirror made at that time as {{ill|Amenohoakari|Q10940411|qid=Q10940411|lt=Amateru Kuniteru Hikohokari-no-Mikoto}}, and this place is therefore called Kagamitsukuri." It is said that this prototype mirror became the shrine's sacred object, and that {{ill|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|Q6080112|qid=Q6080112|lt=Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto}} (who forged the {{ill|Yata no Kagami|Q2610017|qid=Q2610017}} when Amaterasu hid in the {{ill|Amano-Iwato|Q3231835|qid=Q3231835}}) and her father {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Nukado}} no Mikoto were also enshrined here. The ''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wamyosho}}'' records "Kagamitsukuri-go" in {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495}}, {{ill|Shikige district|ja|式下郡|zh|式下郡|qid=Q11486987|lt=Jokage District}}. Since the mirror-making clan (kagamitsukuri-be) is said to have lived here producing mirrors, the shrine's founding is thought to be closely tied to that clan. Nearby shrines such as {{ill|Kagamitsukuri Ita Shrine|Q54153278|qid=Q54153278}} and {{ill|Kagamitsukurimake Shrine|ja|鏡作麻気神社|qid=Q43594607}} are also pointed out as related.
[[ファイル:鏡作坐天照御魂神社 御神宝.jpg|サムネイル|右]]

In {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daido}} 1 ({{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}}), eighteen households were donated as shrine estates (''{{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|Q11502312|qid=Q11502312}}''). In the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}'' it is listed as a major shrine and noted to receive offerings for monthly rites and the {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518|lt=new harvest rite}}.

On {{ill|January 27|Q2284|qid=Q2284}}, {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} 3 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), it was granted divine rank from junior fifth lower to junior fifth upper (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}'') - recorded as "Kagamitsukuri Amateru Mitama no Kami."

From the medieval period onward it was called "Kagamitsukuri Sansho Daimyojin," but is said to have declined until the {{ill|Tawaramoto Domain|Q10425374|qid=Q10425374}} was established in the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} (then a {{ill|kōtai yoriai|Q11373913|qid=Q11373913}} holding of the {{ill|Hirano family|Q11483690|qid=Q11483690|lt=Hirano family}}).

From the Edo period onward, it drew deep devotion from the mirror industry.

After entering the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} era and issuance of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinbutsu Bunri Edict}}, the shrine temple, the {{ill|Shingon Buddhism|bg|Шингон|bn|শিঙ্গোন বৌদ্ধধর্ম|ca|Shingon (budisme)|cs|Šingon|cy|Shingon|da|Shingon Skolen|de|Shingon-shū|eo|Ŝingono|es|Budismo shingon|et|Shingon|eu|Shingon|fa|شینگون|fi|Shingon|fr|Shingon|hu|Singon buddhizmus|id|Buddhisme Shingon|it|Buddismo Shingon|ja|真言宗|ko|진언종|mr|शिंगॉन बौद्ध|nl|Shingon|no|Shingon-shū|pl|Shingon|pt|Shingon|ro|Shingon|ru|Сингон|sh|Shingon budizam|sr|Šingon|sv|Shingon|th|ชิงงง|tr|Şingon Budizmi|uk|Секта Сінґон|vi|Chân ngôn tông|wuu|真言宗|zh|真言宗|zh_classical|真言宗|zh_min_nan|Chin-giân-chong|zh_yue|真言宗|qid=Q550182}} Kangakurin of Iishu-zan Jingū-ji, was abolished. However, its bell tower alone remained and survives to the present.

In April {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} (Meiji 6) it was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, and in {{ill|1936|Q18649|qid=Q18649}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 11) it was ranked as {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=kensha}}.

It possesses the sacred treasure called "three divine mirrors with two beasts."

* Kagami Stone - unearthed from Kagami Pond. It is said to have been used to polish mirror surfaces during mirror making.
* Bell tower - bell tower of Jingū-ji Kangakurin. The {{ill|Bonshō|Q8192099|qid=Q8192099}} was made in {{ill|Kansei|arz|كانسى|de|Kansei|fa|کانسی (دوره)|fr|Ère Kansei|id|Kansei|ja|寛政|ko|간세이|pt|Era Kansei|ru|Кансэй|simple|Kansei|sr|Кансеи|sv|Kansei|tr|Kansei|zh|寬政|qid=Q1195131}} 7 ({{ill|1795|Q7815|qid=Q7815}}). During the {{ill|Pacific War|Q184425|qid=Q184425}} it was surrendered under the {{ill|Metal Collection Order|ja|金属類回収令|qid=Q11646956}}, but the war ended before it was melted and it was safely returned to the shrine.
